card.hook: Picture a square that tilts like a gentle slide, with a Gothic church waiting at the bottom and a town hall tower standing guard on the side. That's Jílové u Prahy, and it fits a phone screen nicely.
card.stand_here: Stand on Masarykovo náměstí in the southern part of the square, looking toward the church of St. Adalbert (sv. Vojtěch) at the lower end of the slope. The town hall tower is beside it, and the wider town centre is behind you to the north.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the whole square. If the tower and church won't both fit, tap 0.5x. Use 2x or more to pick out the tower or the church spire on its own.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the church up with one of the vertical lines so the buildings stay straight.
card.best_time: No best time is confirmed for this view, so just see how the light looks on the day. If the square is busy, take a short burst or a Live Photo and pick the frame with the fewest people in it.
card.selfie_here: Stand on Masarykovo náměstí in front of the church of St. Adalbert, at the lower end of the square. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the church over your shoulder. For a bigger view, the 18 m viewing platform of the Pepř lookout (91 steps) puts the town behind you.
card.ask_someone: Hand your phone to a passer-by on Masarykovo náměstí by the town hall, and stand so the town hall building fills the frame behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The square is open to everyone and needs no ticket. If you want to go inside the church or up the Pepř lookout, check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Get the tower and the church in one straight, level shot, with the slope leading the eye down and a little breathing room around the spire.
card.good_to_know: The town was founded in the 13th century, and its early story is tied to gold mining. The town hall began as a fortress, and its tower dates from the 14th century. The church is the oldest building in town, built in the first half of the 13th century on the site of a wooden church, and scenes from the film Amadeus were shot inside it.

selfie_spots.why: The church is the oldest building in town and sits at the lower end of the main square, so it fills the background well.

selfie_research.notes: The landmark was not named beyond the town itself, so I took the town's main square and its church and town hall as the landmark. No page I found is a selfie guide naming a photo position; the square spot comes from photo and view pages, and the Pepř platform is a viewpoint rather than a landmark photo spot. The given position (49.89806, 14.49278) is roughly 450 m north of the church's listed coordinates, so it may not be the square itself. The ask-someone spot is a suggested square location, not a stated photo point. No page stated rules on selfie sticks or tripods, and none mentioned a safety point.

card.hook: Seven pale stone arches march across a green valley, and your first problem is simply getting all of them into the frame. It's a nice problem to have.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the viaduct: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Stay on public ground, face the arches and keep well away from the railway and its embankment.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x and tilt the phone gently upwards to catch the tall piers and the whole row of arches. Then try 1x, or 2x to 5x if your phone has it, for a single arch or the texture of the stonework.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines and line them up with the piers so the verticals stand up straight instead of leaning.
card.best_time: A bright but slightly overcast day is best, because the soft light shows off the stonework. In strong sun the shadows under the arches get very dark, so tap the sky or stone and slide it brighter or darker until it looks right.
card.selfie_here: Try the small road below the viaduct in the Kocour valley, where the arches rise overhead. Use the front camera at 0.5x with the arches over your shoulder, and check on the spot which way to face, since nothing says exactly where the best angle is.
card.ask_someone: Walk to Žampašská vyhlídka, about 100 m from the marked viewpoint, where bushes and trees don't block the view of the bridge, and ask a passer-by to photograph you with the viaduct in the background.
card.rules_and_safety: Stay on public ground and never walk onto the railway or its embankment. Climbing around the piers from the road is somewhat dangerous, especially on the way back down, so don't do it for a photo.
card.challenge: Take one photo of the whole viaduct and one of a single arch, then see which one your friends like better.
card.good_to_know: At 41.73 m, this is the highest stone bridge in the Czech Republic. It is 109.3 m long, and each of its seven arches is 12 m wide. It was built between 1898 and 1900, mainly by Italian workers, and in 2013 the Czech National Bank put it on a coin.

selfie_spots.why: A source describes this road as a place to view the bridge from below, and a passer-by could frame the visitor against the arches, but no page says where to face to get the viaduct behind a selfie.

selfie_research.notes: No source names a spot with the viaduct directly behind a visitor's selfie; the 'behind' framing for both selfie spots is my inference from the viewpoint and road descriptions, so check on site. The coordinates given match the bridge's listed position. Sources about tripods (a photography guide recommends one) are advice, not rules, so I did not list them. No page states selfie-stick rules. card.hook: Here's a twist: you've come to see rapids, and they're not there. The Štěchovice reservoir flooded them in 1943, so what's left is calm water in a deep, wooded valley, and it's still lovely.
card.stand_here: Stand on Smetanova vyhlídka, the terrace near the Ztracenka campsite area, reached by a branch road from Teletín. Face out over the valley so the river curve and steep slopes fill your screen. Its exact position isn't pinned down, so check the map before you set off.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for a natural view of the valley. Go to 0.5x to fit in more slopes and sky, or 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the curve of the river.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the far hillside on the upper third line with the water below, and keep a bit of terrace edge or a tree in the foreground to show how deep the valley is.
card.best_time: We haven't confirmed a perfect hour for this spot. A clear day helps, and if the sun makes the water glare, try again at a different time of day.
card.selfie_here: Try Vyhlídka Máj, the rocky spur lookout above the horseshoe bend, about a 1 km walk from Teletín. It's one of the most photographed views in the Czech Republic. Use the front camera, try 0.5x to squeeze in more valley, and keep the view over your shoulder while you stand well back from the edge.
card.rules_and_safety: Vyhlídka Máj has no railing or platform, and the pasture on the route is fenced with an electric fence. Stay well back from any drop when you take a picture.
card.challenge: Take a photo where the terrace edge sits in the corner and the river curve winds into the distance, so a friend can see how deep the valley is.
card.good_to_know: The rapids (Svatojánské proudy) were part of the inspiration for Smetana's Má vlast, and they gave their name to an opera by Josef Richard Rozkošný. Smetanova vyhlídka was built for the 150th anniversary of Smetana's birth. It's a quieter alternative to the better-known Vyhlídka Máj.

selfie_spots.name: Vyhlídka Máj lookout, above the Vltava bend near Teletín
selfie_spots.detail: on the rocky spur (skalní ostroh) above the horseshoe meander, reached by a roughly 1 km walk from Teletín
selfie_spots.why: A rock-spur lookout over the bend where the rapids once ran, and one of the most photographed views in the Czech Republic, though the rapids themselves are now under water.

sources.title: Nevíte kam na výlet? Zkuste vyhlídku Máj a vzpomínku na Svatojánské proudy - Médium.cz

selfie_spots.name: Rock with the Ferdinand Column, Třebenice end of the St John's Rapids trail
selfie_spots.detail: on the rock (skála) where the Ferdinand column stands, at the Třebenice end of the educational trail
selfie_spots.why: The Ferdinand column was the main symbol of the rapids and the trail ends in Třebenice, but the column was moved after the reservoirs flooded the site, so the old rapids are not really behind a visitor here.

selfie_research.notes: The rapids no longer exist as visible water: they were flooded by the Štěchovice reservoir (from 1943) and the Slapy reservoir (1955), so no source confirms a spot where the rapids are visible behind a visitor. The Máj lookout looks out over the former rapids, which would place the landmark in front of a visitor rather than behind, and no page gives a precise standing point for a selfie. The Ferdinand column rock is near the trail, not at the water itself. No page gives a standing point for a passer-by photo of the whole landmark, so ask_someone_spot is null. The given coordinates (49.83917, 14.44611) are a few hundred metres from the Wikidata point for the former rapids (49°50'24"N, 14°27'0"E), and the rapids' location is described as at Štěchovice/Třebenice, not Jílové u Prahy itself. No page states selfie-stick or tripod rules or a safety point.

card.hook: Picture a river slicing right through the middle of a village, with a church sitting on the far bank like it's waiting for its portrait. That's Kamenný Přívoz, and the bridge is the best seat in the house.
card.stand_here: Stand on the road bridge, Most Kamenný Přívoz, over the Sázava. Face the church side of the village and look across the water toward the church of St. Ludmila.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the river, the bridge and the village in one go. Go to 0.5x for more valley and sky, then try 2x-5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the church of St. Ludmila.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the river along the lower third line, so the water leads the eye straight to the church.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters the water and the rooftops, but check the light on the day. The bridge works can change what you're able to do, so look around when you arrive.
card.selfie_here: Flip to the front camera and try 0.5x so more of the valley fits in. Turn so the church and river sit over your shoulder, and only do it where it's safe to stand.
card.rules_and_safety: The bridge is under reconstruction until about May 2027, so access and the view from the deck may be restricted. If you can stand on it, take care around traffic and check on site for a safe spot.
card.challenge: Get a shot where the river runs like a road to the church, then zoom in for a close-up of the church and see which one you like better.
card.good_to_know: Kamenný Přívoz sits on the Sázava River in the Central Bohemian Region and has about 1,600 inhabitants. Its German name is Steinüberfuhr, and it's made up of four municipal parts. If you have time for a longer walk, the Žampažská vyhlídka looks across the river toward the Žampach railway viaduct and the weir. It's a trail walk of about 5 km from Jílové u Prahy, so not a quick stop.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot or a passer-by photo spot for Kamenný Přívoz with the landmark in the background. The pages I found are general village, history, transport and photo-archive pages, so I did not invent any spots. Possible leads, not verified as selfie or photo spots: the Commons file titled 'Kamenný Přívoz, pohled z mostu ke kostelu' (a view from the bridge toward the church, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Kamenn%C3%BD_P%C5%99%C3%ADvoz) and the Commons file 'Kamenný Přívoz, obec z mostu' (a view of the village from the bridge, same page). Those titles only show that the bridge over the Sázava is a viewing point. The bridge is also doubtful as a photo spot right now: a Denik article (https://kutnohorsky.denik.cz/kraj-a-okoli/most-pres-sazavu-ceka-demolice-dlouhe-objizdky-potrvaji-az-do-kvetna/) reports a full reconstruction with closure and long detours, and a Seznam result (https://search.seznam.cz/?q=mosty+p%C5%99es+s%C3%A1zavu&sId=fEHX9TO7MIKTqDX8IO6R&sourceid=web&thru=related) says traffic restrictions on it last until the end of 2026. Check the current status on site before going. The '1 Jílové u Prahy' town-side details also do not name a selfie location. Also, no page I found gives selfie-stick or tripod rules or a safety point for this site. Because the search was limited, a local check or a dedicated photo-spot search may still find a named spot.
